resources.string: CellWatch is an FCC Challenge app. You can collect measurements to send to the FCC to show that your coverage doesn’t meet the minimum standards, or take measurements to test speeds for yourself.
¿Prefiere español? Se puede cambiar el idioma en los ajustes del dispositivo.

To formally challenge a provider’s performance claims, you need to take several measurements within a geographic area and submit them to the FCC, the U.S. government agency that regulates telecommunications.
Our app helps consumers take these measurements and automatically submits them to the FCC.

A challenge to a provider’s coverage claims is specific to a geographic area. The FCC has used a hexagonal tiling system to define regions. By collecting several measurements within one hexagonal region, a consumer can prove that the region does not have good mobile Internet performance, despite what their cell carrier may claim.
Our app shows two layers of hexagonal regions: each large hexagonal region contains seven (7) child hexagons.
Challenges are for the larger hexagons, and you must take measurements within a specific number of child hexagons to count as a challenge.
The data you collect with CellWatch will be shared with the public, including the general location and time of your measurements.
Your CellWatch data may also be used for research purposes.
Please read our privacy policy for details.

Would you like to work towards a formal FCC challenge? You can update this later in the app settings.\n\nIn both modes your data will be shared with the public, including general locations and timestamps, and may be used by the CellWatch team for research purposes.
Measurements will be sent to the FCC as challenge data. The FCC may make public your exact GPS location, provider, and other relevant details.
Measurements will not be sent to the FCC.
If you would like to work toward an official FCC challenge, this information must be submitted to the FCC with your measurements. This information will never be shared with the public.
I acknowledge that my service provider may share necessary customer-specific information with the FCC (such as IP address and service plan details).

In order to take measurements, we need the following permissions:

1. Location, to know where measurements are taken.

2. Phone calls, to gather information about your cellular connection. We will never make phone calls.
When ready, click the button below and grant permissions when prompted. You can update these permissions later in your device\'s settings.
Are you standing outdoors or in a moving vehicle?
By clicking "Go", I certify to the best of my ability that:
I am a subscriber of the provider being challenged
My phone is in working order
All statements in this submission are true and correct
You are currently in Testing mode, so this measurement will not be submitted to the FCC. You can change the collection mode in Settings.
All data will be stored and used consistent with our privacy policy.
It looks like you are connected to WiFi or have cellular data disabled. If you proceed, your measurement may not be submitted to the FCC.
Cannot enable FCC Challenge mode without setting name, phone, and email.
Cannot set a blank name, phone number, or email while in FCC Challenge mode.

The CellWatch app is part of the CellWatch open-source cellular network measurement suite created by researchers at the Georgia Institute of Technology; the University of California, Santa Barbara; and Northern Arizona University. CellWatch is generously funded by the Rockefeller Foundation.
Learn more at our website: sites.gatech.edu/cellwatch.
CellWatch is built with many open source libraries. Most of their licenses and required notices are included in an autogenerated list accessible via the button below.
